**Tier:** 3
Formulas BPFO = N/2·fr(1−Bd/Pd·cosφ), BPFI = N/2·fr(1+Bd/Pd·cosφ), BSF = Pd/(2Bd)·fr(1−(Bd/Pd·cosφ)²), FTF = fr/2(1−Bd/Pd·cosφ); "a defect on the element strikes a race twice per spin, so the observed ball-defect frequency is usually 2 × BSF"; slip "shifts the actual frequencies one to two percent below the kinematic prediction"; bearing frequencies are "not integer multiples of shaft speed".

## Case reports (forums and mailing lists)

**[15]** Watt, Dan; OzAndrewJ (Andrew Johansen). "EQ6 w/ Rowan Belts RA Spike." *Cloudy Nights*, 1–17 Feb 2023.
<https://www.cloudynights.com/forums/topic/861819-eq6-w-rowan-belts-ra-spike/>
**Tier:** 4 — **Access:** operator-supplied
Legacy EQ6 with Rowan belts: "RA spike every 133 seconds"; had "replaced the bearings with better ones from deepspaceproducts"; three teardowns, backlash/float/preload changes, spur-gear reinstall, pulley swap, RA/DEC motor swap all failed. OzAndrewJ: "The worm period is 478.7 seconds and the motor period is 122.2 seconds … If you run an unguided test, and the period becomes 122 seconds then its more than likely a slight eccentricity in the mounting of the pulley on the motor." Fix: "It was the "upgraded" ceramic worm gear bearings … when I popped the original 608 bearings back in all of my weird spikes disappeared and I'm back to guiding at .4 RMS."

**[16]** Chris; Hoskin, Robert. "Periodic spike in RA during guiding." *MOUNTS@ESPMC-Eight.groups.io*, 21–22 May 2022.

**Tier:** 4 — **Access:** operator-supplied
Explore Scientific Exos2-GT PMC-8 (not Sky-Watcher): "Every ~134s the error goes from within ~1.5 arc-sec to over 5 (and sometimes as high as 9) arc-sec. It recovers very quickly, usually within a second or two." Hoskin: "Your spike is on the period of the small pulley of the belt drive". Changes before the fix report: recentred/tensioned an off-centre, loose belt and tightened worm gear slop on shaft; the next post also reports re-plugging the RA serial cable and "a bunch of time getting my polar alignment just right", then "The spikes in RA are completely gone". Which change removed the spike is not isolated.

## Diagnosis tools and method

**[33]** Waddington, Bruce. "Analyzing PHD2 Guiding Results – A Basic Tutorial" (V1.1, Jan 2016). *Open PHD Guiding*.
<https://openphdguiding.org/Analyzing_PHD2_Guide_Logs.pdf>
**Tier:** 2
Look whether a big move started with a large guide command (PHD2-induced) or was followed by corrections (mechanical); push/tug test on guide scope and cables; run Guiding Assistant with guiding disabled "at least as long as the worm period in your mount".

**[34]** Open PHD Guiding. "Trouble-shooting and Analysis" (PHD2 manual).
<https://www.openphdguiding.org/man-dev/Trouble_shooting.htm>
**Tier:** 2
Most abrupt deflections "arise from neither the mount nor PHD2's guide commands"; RA "unusually large, randomly space[d] deflections are more likely to arise from the sorts of mechanical problems described here than from errors in the RA drive system"; "a movement of only 5 microns can create an apparent tracking error (guide star deflection) of over 6 arc-sec". Measuring-the-mount protocol: new profile, guide speed 0.5–1x, 2 s exposures near Dec 0, GA 10–15 min.

**[35]** Galasso, Andy. "PHD2 Log Viewer." *adgsoftware.com*.
<https://www.adgsoftware.com/phd2utils/>
**Tier:** 2
"Identify RA drive harmonics by looking at the RA frequency analysis"; excludes post-dither settling. FFT window/resolution not documented on the page.

**[36]** EQMOD Project. "PECPrep Periodic Error Analysis and PEC Generation — User Guide."
<https://eq-mod.sourceforge.net/docs/PECPrep.pdf>
**Tier:** 2
"the 470 second peak listed will actually correspond to the 479s worm period" (bin quantisation); resolution slider trades bin width vs short-period range; period slider can be changed "if you want to isolate other periodic signals"; phase column "useful for identifying elements that originate from the same mechanical source"; "If you find that odd harmonics are particularly prominent this might indicate that the associated mechanical part is being restricted in its movement"; capture "at least 5 times the worm period … For an EQ6 this 40 mins" with guiding off. Legacy EQ6 example: worm 479 s, transfer gear 366 s, stepper spur 122 s.

**[37]** EQMOD Project. "PECPrep" page.
<https://eq-mod.sourceforge.net/pecprep/>
**Tier:** 2
"PECPrep is able to filter wind, seeing effects, linear and non linear drift to isolate the periodic signal associated with a mounts worm drive."

**[38]** Herman, Michael. "Measuring Periodic Error in Telescope Mounts" (v2, 9 Dec 2022). Losmandy_users groups.io attachment.
<https://groups.io/g/Losmandy_users/attachment/83000/0/Periodic+Error+Measurement+in+Telescope+Mounts+by+Michael+Herman+December+9+2022+v2.pdf>
**Tier:** 3
Unguided PE run: calibrate, then restart PHD2 with "Enable Mount Guide Output" unchecked, 1–2 s exposures ~45–50 min, analyse in PECPrep with AutoFilter. Losmandy cases: gearbox vibration at worm/7.5 "cannot be corrected by PEC"; "a ball in a RA worm block bearing getting pinched". PE testing alone cannot identify the part — swap parts and re-measure.

**[39]** open-astro. "OpenAstro Guide Insight." *GitHub*.
<https://github.com/open-astro/openastro-guide-insight/>
**Tier:** 3
Fork of PHD2 Log Viewer; analyse selection/GA run/session for periodic error and "export the periodogram as CSV".

**[40]** EQMOD Project. "Mount Periodic Error Correction through Variable Track Speed Adjustment."
<https://eq-mod.sourceforge.net/eqspeed.htm>
**Tier:** 2
PE "caused by runout or gear teeth spacing discrepancies in the mount's RA wormgears"; "on a EQ6 mount, the rotation cycle is 8 minutes."
